title: Bye, inversions!
source_text: Given an array $a$ of $n$ integers. You need to swap adjacent numbers exactly $k$ times. The goal is to minimise the number of inversions after exactly $k$ swaps. An inversion is a pair $(i, j)$ such that $i < j$ and $a_{i} > a_{j}$ ### Input - The first line contains an integer $T$ indicating the number of test cases. For each test case, there are two lines in total. - The first line contains two space separated integers - $n$ and $k$. - The second line contains $n$ space separated integers, the $i^{th}$ of which is $a_i$. ### Output Output $T$ lines in total. Each line should start with "Case #: " and followed by the minimum inversions after swaps. Here "#" is the number of the test case starting from $1$. ### Constraints - $1 \leq T \leq 10$ - $2 \leq n \leq 100000$ - $0 \leq k \leq 1000000$ - $1 \leq a_{i} \leq n$ ### Example Input ``` 3 3 3 3 2 1 3 1 1 2 3 3 2 1 2 3 ``` ### Example Output: ``` Case 1: 0 Case 2: 1 Case 3: 0 ``` ### Explanation **Test Case 1:** $(3 2) 1$ --> $2 3 1$ --> $2 (3 1)$ --> $2 1 3$ --> $(2 1) 3$ --> $1 2 3$ **Test Case 2:** $(1 2) 3$ --> $2 1 3$.
